title: Peer view
description: What `wipctl peers --json` emits: every plan this one declares, whether it is attached, and which entries here depend on it. This is the verb's output shape, not the section a project writes — the peers half of plan.schema.json is that section. The view opens no url: it reads the table, this record's lane files, and the slot of each attached peer, so its answer is a function of committed files on this machine.

alias.description: The row's key: the local name this plan gives the peer.

plan_id.description: The peer's plan_id, as the row states it.

urls.description: The row's locations, in the row's own order.

attached.description: Whether a slot on this machine holds the plan this plan_id names.

slot.description: Absolute path of the slot holding the peer. Present when attached and absent otherwise, because a field is absent rather than null where the state does not have it.

revision.description: The commit the view read the peer at, in the record's own revision form. Present when attached and absent otherwise. Two machines that answer differently differ here, which is what makes the disagreement one line to diagnose.

stale.description: True when no dependency in this record uses the alias. A stale row breaks nothing and misleads a reader, so it is reported and never failed. This is derived from the references below rather than stated beside them, so the two agree by conditional: stale is true exactly when the reference list is empty.

references.description: Every dependency in this record that reaches into this peer, empty when none.

entry.description: This record's entry that carries the dependency.

target.description: The peer's entry it depends on, without the alias prefix: the alias is the row this reference sits under.

lane.description: The lane the target sits in. Present when the peer is attached and the target is live, and absent otherwise.

target_state.description: What the peer's record says about the target. Present when the peer is attached and absent otherwise, because an unattached peer answers nothing. A deleted or renamed target is read from that peer's tombstones rather than guessed at.

successor.description: The id that replaced the target. Present when target_state is renamed and absent otherwise.
